title: Spring flow gave no clear added late-season low-flow prediction gain at three Arctic gauges in 1980-2011
abstract: We tested whether May-June mean flow improves an August-October minimum seven-day flow estimate after July flow and a linear time trend are known. We used ArcticGRO v20261104 at Ob-Salekhard, Lena-Kyusyur and Yenisey-Igarka. Each fit used earlier certified years from 1936. In 31 common test years in 1980-2011, adding spring flow raised pooled mean squared log error by 1.76%. The conditional 95% three-year block interval for error reduction was -11.99% to +8.11%. Root mean squared log error changed from 0.29714 to 0.29974. All planned checks were also uncertain. This gives no clear added gain for these models. It does not show that spring storage has no effect. Revised records, retrospective certification, regulation, short coverage and conditional uncertainty limit inference. Code, aggregate scores, source hashes, a figure and an independent numerical audit support reproduction. Raw records and record-level tables remain external.

display.caption: Added spring-flow error reduction in the primary test and planned checks. Positive values indicate lower error. Lines show conditional 95% three-year paired block limits.
